chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said:
I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Is it allowed for the one in Ihram to walk under the shade of the carriage?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

He (the narrator) said, 'And a man asked him (peace be upon him) about the shade for the one in Ihram, from the harm of rain or sun, and I was listening. So he (peace be upon him) ordered him that he should expiate with a sheep, and slaughter it at Mina'.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling for an Ihram pilgrim walking under a carriage versus seeking shade from rain or sun?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam al-Rida’s (AS) nuanced distinction between permissible shade and shade sought for specific relief, which necessitates an expiation (fidyah). While walking under a carriage is allowed without penalty, seeking shelter from rain or sun specifically triggers the obligation to slaughter a sheep at Mina, reflecting the juristic principle of linking certain acts of convenience during Ihram to compensatory sacrifices. This ruling underscores the balance between ease and ritual purity in Shia fiqh regarding the state of Ihram.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie who said,
‘I wrote to Al-Rezaasws, ‘Is it allowed for the one in Ihraam if he walks under a shade of the carriage?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And a man asked himasws about the shade for the one in Ihraam, from the harm of rain, or sun, and I was listening. So heasws ordered him that he should expiate with a sheep, and slaughter it at Mina’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Isma‘il ibn Bazi’ who has said the following: “I wrote to al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked if it is permissible to walk in the shadow of the carriage on camel back. He (the Imam) wrote back, ‘Yes, it is permissible.’

Another man had asked about preparing a shadow for one in the state of Ihram because of rain or sun and I was listening, he (the Imam) commanded him to pay a ransom of one sheep to be slaughtered in Mina.”
